activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix in the General Case

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{-7}$ and ${V}_{-2}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =-7$ and $\lambda =-2$ of $A$, respectively?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 \\ -2 & -8-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(-8-\lambda )+6)=0 \\ -(\lambda +2)({\lambda }^{2}+9\lambda +14)=0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +7)=0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2}(\lambda +7)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=-2$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=-7$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =-7.$ Since ${V}_{-7}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-7})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda =-2,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{-2},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-(-2)I)\text{x}=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-2})=2.
$$
